text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Soldier killed, eight wounded in Lebanon.
- Ehud Barak wins big at Labour party convention.
- Northern Israeli commander Amiram Levine warns Hizbollah.
- U.S. Secretary of State-designate Madeline Albright says Middle East envoy Dennis Ross doing a "brilliant job".
- Israeli army using soldiers as guinea pigs in nerve gas antidote experiments.
- Zim's general manager Matty Morganstern resigns following $2.1 million losses.
- Cabinet approves most structural reforms in public sector blueprint.
- Rogovin family sells ownership of building firm for $30 million to two groups of investors headed by businessmen Ezra Hakhshouri and Yossi Granot.
- Tadiran Telecommunications receives $15 million order from Belgacom, the Belgian telecom provider.
- Israeli holiday islands on Mediterranean move a step closer.
GLOBES
- Government approves main structural changes. Stock exchange refuses to fall -- light rise. Currency basket against the shekel at its lowest level in half a year.
- Intel unveils modernised "Pentium" developed in Israel with an investment of $100 million.
HAARETZ
- Soldier killed in Lebanon.
- Albright tells Senate: I'll do all that's required to bring comprehensive peace to the Middle East.
- Labour party accepts Barak's proposal: Chairman will be elected only by party members.
- Late Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin charged the United States -- without his agreement -- told Syrian President Hafez al-Assad of Israel's readiness to withdraw from the Golan.
- Police investigators learn to identify liars with help of videotaped interview Netanyahu's wife gave television.
MAARIV
- Deterioration in Lebanon: Soldier killed, Katyusha fired at western Galilee.
- Netanyahu in negotiations with Palestinians -- "We have patience".
- Initiative in Netanyahu's office: Bank Hapoalim group will be broken up before the sale.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Crisis in Hebron talks.
- Trade Minister Natan Sharansky going to Russia on 26 January.

- Former Shin Bet head Avraham Shalom says then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir knew everything about Bus 300 affair in which two Palestinian prisoners were killed. Shamir: He didn't admit it before ordering the killings.
